name: Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma Data Center

profile.reading: This is a data facility tagged to the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma in south Durant, Oklahoma, most likely referring to information technology infrastructure housed within the tribes new administrative headquarters building, a five story, 500,000 square foot facility on an 80 acre campus in south Durant that opened in June 2018 and houses various tribal government offices and service centers. The Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma is a federally recognized Native American tribal government operating as a republic with executive, legislative, and judicial branches, led by an elected chief, with a twelve member unicameral Tribal Council representing the nations twelve districts; the de jure tribal capital remains Tuskahoma, Oklahoma, where the Tribal Council continues to meet monthly, even though day to day administration is based at this newer Durant headquarters. As of 2020 census data, the Choctaw Nations jurisdictional area held about 226,984 people, with total tribal enrollment at roughly 223,279 members, of whom about 84,670 enrolled citizens live in Oklahoma. No specific power capacity in megawatts or dedicated data center square footage distinct from the overall administrative building total was found in sourcing checked this session, an honest gap this registry records rather than estimates.
profile.research_note: Fresh research via Wikipedia, the only source reachable this session after web search quota exhaustion. Building_sqft reflects the whole administrative headquarters building, not a dedicated data center space specifically, since no more granular figure was found; noted honestly in the reading.

reading.body:
This facility is attributed to the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma in Durant, Oklahoma, but its specifications are not published. The site's research was exhausted without confirming whether a dedicated data center exists at this location or finding any technical specifications, power capacity, or cooling capability. A tribal headquarters building opened there in 2018 alongside various government services and tribal enterprises including document archiving, but no sourcing confirmed a data center facility or its infrastructure.

Oklahoma has no published capacity figures from any data center operator on record with this site. Nine facilities are mapped in the state, but none report their power draw publicly. This location cannot be ranked against other sites in the state or region because the capacity is unknown.

Without published specifications, this campus cannot be assessed for relevance to AI scaling. The absence of a confirmed facility or stated power capacity means it does not yet appear in any measurable capacity analysis of the US AI infrastructure landscape.
